card.occupation: Co-owner and managing director of two franchised bubble tea outlets in Plymouth city centre. She works about 12 hours a week, mostly on rotas, stock orders, supplier calls and checking the books. A full-time shift supervisor handles the day-to-day.
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school (SPM, then STPM) in Ipoh, Malaysia. Moved to the UK at 18 and took a BSc in Business Management at the University of Plymouth, graduating with a 2:1 in 2014. Has done food hygiene and franchise operations courses since. No postgraduate study, and no interest in any.
card.household: Rents a three-bed new-build semi in Plymstock with her partner Tom, 35, a marine engineer at Devonport. They've been together seven years and aren't married. Neither feels much need to be. No children. They have a grey British Shorthair called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Malaysian Chinese, born and raised in Ipoh, Perak. Her parents run a small hardware shop there and her older brother lives in Kuala Lumpur. She grew up speaking Cantonese at home and Malay and English at school. She was raised loosely Buddhist-Taoist through her grandparents but has no religion herself and only keeps the family side of Chinese New Year. She got British citizenship in 2022 and thinks of Plymouth as home now, though she calls Malaysia 'back home' when talking about family.
card.professional_persona: Practical and money-focused. She opened the first unit in 2019 with savings, a loan from her dad and Tom as guarantor, then added a second in 2022. She likes being the boss and having 'Director' on Companies House, but doesn't want to work long hours if she doesn't have to. She's good at haggling with suppliers and landlords and isn't shy about pushing for a better deal. She'll take a shortcut on paperwork if she thinks nobody will check. Staff find her fair but brisk.
card.sports_persona: Goes to a PureGym three times a week, mostly treadmill and weights machines, headphones in. She isn't sporty in a team sense. She'll go to Home Park with Tom a couple of times a season for the atmosphere and a pint, but couldn't name many Argyle players. Does the odd 5k charity run if a friend asks.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person. She watches Netflix and reality TV (Love Island, Selling Sunset, Married at First Sight Australia) and the occasional Korean drama her mum recommends. Listens to whatever's on Spotify's Today's Top Hits in the car. She's been to the Theatre Royal for a musical once or twice, usually because someone bought tickets for a birthday.
card.travel_persona: Flies back to Malaysia roughly every 18 months to two years for two or three weeks, usually via Doha. Otherwise she likes easy, comfortable holidays: all-inclusive in Tenerife or Turkey, a long weekend in London for shopping and a nice dinner. Not interested in backpacking or 'finding herself'. She likes a good hotel and a pool.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks simple home-style Chinese and Malaysian dishes a few times a week: rice, stir-fried veg, steamed fish, curry chicken when she can be bothered. She buys from the Oriental supermarket near the city centre and complains that you can't get proper Ipoh bean sprout chicken or decent char kway teow in Plymouth. Tom cooks roasts and pasta. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Likes a Sunday carvery more than she lets on.
hobbies_and_interests: gym sessions with podcasts or playlists
browsing and buying skincare, mostly Korean and Japanese brands
Vinted and eBay for selling clothes she's bored of
keeping an eye on property prices on Rightmove
weekend walks on Plymouth Hoe or out at Wembury with Tom
video calls with her mum on Sundays
skills: staff rota planning and basic HR
reading a lease and spotting a bad clause
stock forecasting for a small food business
card.career_goals: Wants to open a third unit, possibly in Exeter, without increasing her own hours much. Longer term she'd like to own a couple of buy-to-let flats so the money comes in without her being there. She'd happily sell the franchise units for a good price in five or ten years. She isn't interested in climbing a corporate ladder. She wants to be comfortable and in charge of her own time.
card.voice: Clear, fairly quick, matter-of-fact. Her accent is mostly Malaysian English softened by 14 years in the South West: slightly clipped consonants, some Malaysian rhythm. She's picked up British phrasing like 'to be fair', 'sort of', 'proper busy' and 'I'm knackered'. Uses 'erm' when thinking, ends points with 'yeah' or 'you know'. Says 'sorry?' if she didn't catch something, without fuss. Doesn't fill silences nervously. She'll just wait or say 'yeah, that's it really'. Occasionally lets a 'lah' slip when she's relaxed or laughing, then carries on as if nothing happened. Gives short, direct answers unless asked about money, business or something she has a firm opinion on.
card.typing: Quick and practical. Usually starts with a capital, but often drops full stops at the end and skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its fine'). Uses 'tbh', 'ok' and 'thx'. Rarely uses emojis in forms. Answers are short, sometimes a single phrase, unless the question is about work.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough but businesslike and a bit guarded at first. She's confident, doesn't get flustered, and isn't trying hard to be liked. Can come across as slightly blunt or pleased with herself when she mentions owning a business. She warms up if the conversation turns to something practical she knows about. Not much for small talk about feelings or abstract ideas.
small_things: the cat knocking things off the kitchen counter
how much the parking costs in the city centre
a new skincare serum she's trying
the gym being packed in January
staff calling in sick on a Saturday
the Oriental supermarket running out of her usual soy sauce brand
rain on the Hoe ruining a weekend walk
a Vinted sale that went for more than she expected
deeper_things: Her dad still talks about the loan as if she owes him the business, and it gets under her skin
Her cousins in Singapore earn far more than she does and she quietly keeps score
She isn't sure she wants children, and Tom's mum keeps hinting
She doesn't really miss Malaysia day to day and sometimes feels guilty that she doesn't
She and Tom have never bothered to marry and she's not sure she ever will, partly because she likes keeping her finances separate
She worried more than she admitted when one unit nearly closed during a slow winter
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, showing head and shoulders. The light comes mostly from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed and there's a faint warm cast from a ceiling light. East Asian woman in her early thirties with straight black shoulder-length hair tucked behind one ear and light, neat makeup. She has a slight, composed half-smile, looking directly into the camera. No glasses. She wears a plain dusky-pink crewneck sweatshirt with small gold stud earrings. Behind her is a light grey painted wall in an open-plan kitchen-diner. A white IKEA shelf holds a small potted snake plant, a stack of three folders labelled in marker, and a jar of chopsticks. To the right, the edge of a grey L-shaped sofa is visible with a mustard cushion, and on the sofa arm a grey cat is half out of frame. A wall calendar with handwritten shift notes hangs slightly crooked near the doorway.
